{% raw %}
`cat`: concatenate files and print them.

## Synopsis

<strong>cat</strong> \[<em>file</em>...\]

## Description

<strong>cat</strong> writes the contents of each <em>file</em> to standard output, one after another. With no <em>file</em>, or where a <em>file</em> is <strong>-</strong>, it reads standard input.

Each read takes what the file has now and writes it at once, so a file that never ends (a sensor's, <strong>/dev/motion0</strong>: an event a line) shows each piece as it comes.

A file that cannot be opened or read is reported on standard error, and <strong>cat</strong> goes on with the next one.

## Options

None.

## Exit status

0 if every file was read; 1 if any could not be opened or read.

## Examples

```text
cat notes.txt
cat head.txt - tail.txt > all.txt
cat /dev/motion0
```

## Notes

GNU <strong>cat</strong>'s options (<strong>-n</strong>, <strong>-A</strong> and the others) are not supported.

## See also

<strong>head</strong>(1), <strong>tail</strong>(1), <strong>less</strong>(1)
